subject: Renewal: dynamic consumption smoothing & tiered discount amendment
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@cambridgeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — proposal for consumption smoothing + tiered discounts

Hi Danielle,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Per our conversation, Cambridge is approaching the renewal window (term ends 2026-06-30) and you mentioned wanting predictable unit economics during peak season while keeping the option to scale capacity.

Attached is a short proposal sketch that aims to balance those needs:
- A soft monthly usage floor (60% of current run-rate) that guarantees a baseline rate and reduces month-to-month volatility for Cambridge.
- Dynamic discount bands that increase with committed monthly consumption (three bands: 60-99%, 100-149%, 150%+) with step-up credits if you exceed a band mid-quarter.
- An overage escrow (cap at 10% of committed spend per quarter) where we provide temporary credits that can be reconciled at true-up.
- Optional 12-month or 24-month term with escalating credit incentives for the longer term.

This structure preserves flexibility for you while giving Redwood enough predictability to offer deeper per-token pricing. I flagged the specific pricing and credit math in the attached term sheet (v3).

Could you confirm whether Cambridge procurement needs a fixed PO cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether we should model invoicing over calendar months or by your fiscal quarter? I can loop in finance to align the invoice/PO flow.

If it helps, I’ll bring Ben (head of renewals) into the thread to finalize the discount tiers and Neha to confirm invoice timing.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm PO cadence and any internal approval milestones this week.
2) We send a redlineable term sheet (attached) + SOW for your legal and procurement.
3) Sign and kick off a phased onboarding for new capacity (if you choose to step up).

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Aisha,

Thanks — this looks promising and closer to what we discussed. A couple of quick clarifications from procurement:
- We prefer monthly POs if possible. Quarterly invoicing complicates our internal accruals.
- The escrow idea is interesting but procurement will need a clear cap and reconciliation window (we prefer 30 days post-quarter).
- Any credits need to be expirations tracked (we can’t accept open-ended credits).

Also, can you do a worked example for April–June with our usage profile (I can send the CSV if that helps)? We need to present to finance on Friday.

If you loop in Ben and Neha now that’s great — thank you.

—Danielle

Thanks Danielle — looping in finance and CS to nail the mechanics. A few notes from the renewal side:

1) Worked example: Aisha, I’ll run the April–June worked example with Cambridge’s CSV once Danielle sends it. For framing, we typically model: committed band discounts applied monthly with a quarterly true-up. You asked for monthly PO cadence — we can invoice monthly but reconcile credit at quarter close (30-day window).

2) Escrow and credits: We can cap the escrow to 10% of committed quarterly spend with a 30-day reconciliation. Credits that aren’t used by reconciliation will expire per the credit schedule in the term sheet (90 days).

3) Overage path: If Cambridge exceeds the highest tier by more than 20% for two consecutive months, we offer an automatic rate review and temporary burst pricing that’s grandfathered for 60 days to give you time to commit to a higher band. That avoids surprise invoices and gives you runway to decide on term extension.

4) Longer terms: 24-month commitment unlocks an additional 3% effective discount and an onboarding credit equal to one month of committed spend. We can put that into the SOW as a separate line item.

Action items for us (assigned):
- Ben: finalize discount band percentages and new worked example (ETA: Thu 4/23 EOD).
- Neha: confirm invoicing cadence and whether monthly invoicing with quarterly true-up requires any additional paperwork on our side (ETA: Thu 4/23).
- Monica: prep a short ops note on how burst capacity onboarding would work (ETA: Fri 4/24).

Danielle — if that plan looks okay I’ll produce a redlineable term sheet and send a DocuSign link for procurement + legal.

Best,
Ben Carter

Attached is the worked example for Apr–Jun using the usage you shared and the redlineable term sheet (v4). Key takeaways from the model:
- If Cambridge opts for a 12-month term with the proposed bands, effective blended rate becomes ~12% lower year-over-year; for 24 months it’s ~15% lower.
- Under the monthly PO + quarterly reconcile: we model monthly invoices; credits are applied as separate line items at quarter close.
- Escrow cap modeled at 10% of quarterly committed spend, with a 30-day reconciliation window. Unused escrow credits expire after 90 days.

I also added a short operational appendix describing the burst onboarding steps (Monica — happy to take your edits).

If Cambridge signs a 24-month term we’ll include a one-month onboarding credit line in the SOW (placed as a negative invoice line).
